newsitem.title: UK: Govt wants Eurotunnel to start wagon design study.
newsitem.headline: Govt wants Eurotunnel to start wagon design study.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc bosses have been summoned to a meeting with the UK's deputy prime minister later on Monday where they will be asked to give an undertaking to carry out a review into ways of making their freight wagons safer.

John Prescott, deputy prime minister and head of the transport and environment super-ministry, will make his request to the Channel Tunnel operator's joint chairmen Robert Malpas and Patrick Ponsolle at a meeting in London this afternoon.

A Department of Transport official told Reuters, "He (Prescott) wants Eurotunnel to consider options for changing the open-sided wagons. Eurotunnel must go away and consider whether there have been sufficient advances in technology in recent years to make the wagons safer."

Eurotunnel's existing open-sided design was blamed for fanning the flames of last November's blaze by the fire chiefs. But the group has resisted a change in design on the grounds of heavy costs at a time when it is laden with nine billion in debt.
It also argues that enclosing the wagons to reduce the fire risk would make them too high for the tunnel and break weight restrictions for track safety.

The deputy PM will also use the meeting to press for a Eurotunnel timetable for implementing the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority's recommendations detailed in its fire report. Eurotunnel will not be able to resume freight services until those recommendations are in place.
The final decision on when Eurotunnel can resume these services will be taken by the Intergovernmental Commission, which consists of advisers from the French and British governments.
Therefore, Prescott's requests will be key to Eurotunnel getting clearance.
Some industry sources now say that it is unlikely the Commission will give its verdict before next week.
